text: Accepted runtime baselines should be centralized in a small helper module to avoid scattered fixed-count assumptions across the test suite. When each smoke test hardcodes its own expected JSONL record counts and FAISS id totals, accepted memory growth forces redundant repairs in multiple files. A single helper such as tests/smoke/_accepted_runtime_baseline.py stores the current front identifier, commit short hash, and canonical counts. Tests import this helper and assert against its values rather than embedding stale numbers. When a new ingestion front advances memory, updating one helper propagates the baseline to all consumers. This pattern was validated in the 09B closeout where three legacy tests were aligned by referencing a shared baseline, proving maintainability and reducing future repair burden.
summary: Centralize accepted baselines in a single helper to avoid scattered assumptions
